first_impression.reaction: Googled 'who can perform a marriage' on the train because my fiance's brother keeps saying he'll 'just do the ceremony' when we marry in Australia. The first two sentences answer it: has to be an authorised celebrant, four types, dated this month. Takeaways then answer my actual question about the brother. I kept going to the friend section, the JP FAQ and the overseas bit, and I'd bookmark it.

journey.quote: As at November 2026, you must be married by an authorised marriage celebrant to be legally married here.
journey.reaction: Straight answer, with a date on it, in the first lines. That's exactly what I wanted.

journey.quote: When the legal side is settled, [Wedded Concierge](https://weddedwonderland.com/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=who-can-perform-a-marriage&utm_content=primary) can take on the celebration.
journey.reaction: A plug before the takeaways. One sentence, so I thumb past it, but it's early.

journey.quote: A friend or family member can only legally marry you once registered as a celebrant, and assessment can take up to 6 months.
journey.reaction: That's my real question answered in the takeaways. Screenshot for my fiance, so he can break it to his brother.

journey.section: Who can legally perform a marriage in Australia?
journey.quote: Section 41 of the Act is headed "Marriages to be solemnised by authorised celebrant".
journey.reaction: I don't need the section heading of an Act. The next sentence says it in plain words, so this one is just in the way.

journey.quote: The two Commonwealth types share one regulator and one register, which is why they are sometimes grouped as a single type, with three groups in all.
journey.reaction: Wait, four types or three? You just told me four, twice. Had to reread this on a small screen and I'm still not sure why it's here.

journey.section: Can a friend or family member marry you?
journey.quote: Only if they become an authorised celebrant first.
journey.reaction: Heading is my exact question and the first line answers it. Perfect.

journey.section: Can a friend or family member marry you?
journey.quote: If a sibling or close friend is set on it, raise it well over a year before the wedding, because the notice must also reach the celebrant at least one month before the day.
journey.reaction: Practical and honest. Also the reading or welcome idea after it gives the brother a role without the paperwork. Good.

journey.section: How to check your celebrant is authorised
journey.quote: Check before you pay a deposit. It takes a few minutes on the official register.
journey.reaction: Numbered steps with the official link. Easy to follow on a phone.

journey.section: Lodging the Notice of Intended Marriage
journey.quote: Our separate guide to the Notice of Intended Marriage takes the form step by step.
journey.reaction: Great, where is it? There's no link here, and that's exactly the next thing I'd tap.

journey.section: What your celebrant must do to make it legal
journey.quote: The celebrant keeps the celebrant copy of the official certificate for six years from the date of the marriage.
journey.reaction: This whole section is more than I came for. Headings are clear so I scrolled past most of it.

journey.section: Who can marry you if your wedding is overseas?
journey.quote: Not your Australian celebrant, at least not legally.
journey.reaction: Clear. The two-path bullets underneath are easy to scan. Didn't know 'legal at home, party abroad' was a normal thing.

journey.section: Who can marry you if your wedding is overseas?
journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor plans the venue, travel, vendors and payments for the celebration abroad as your single point of contact, in your time zone and quoting in AUD, while the legal ceremony stays with you and your celebrant: speak with [Wedded Concierge](https://weddedwonderland.com/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=who-can-perform-a-marriage&utm_content=secondary).
journey.reaction: Very long sentence for a phone, and 'Wedded Advisor' appears out of nowhere. Not sure who that is.

journey.quote: Can a Justice of the Peace marry you in Australia?
journey.reaction: My mum asked exactly this. Short, direct answer. FAQ questions are the things I'd actually type into Google.

unanswered_questions: Where is the Notice of Intended Marriage guide the page mentions? I couldn't find a link to it.
Who is a Wedded Advisor, and is that the same as Wedded Concierge?
Do you work with couples who live outside Australia, like us in Singapore?

turn_offs_found.quote: The two Commonwealth types share one regulator and one register, which is why they are sometimes grouped as a single type, with three groups in all.
turn_offs_found.why: The page told me four types in the intro and takeaways, then this line says three. On a phone that makes me doubt the number I came for, and it doesn't help me pick anyone.

turn_offs_found.quote: Our separate guide to the Notice of Intended Marriage takes the form step by step.
turn_offs_found.why: It promises the next answer I'd want and then gives me nothing to tap. I'd have to go back to Google, and I might not come back.

would_share_with: My fiance, for the friend or family member section, to pass to his brother
My mum, for the Justice of the Peace answer

cta_reaction.why: I came to find out if my fiance's brother can marry us, not for a planner. The links weren't pushy and nothing blocked the content. If we went with 'legal at home, celebrate abroad', I'd come back. For now, bookmark.

top_3_changes: Remove or move to the body footnote the 'sometimes grouped as a single type, with three groups in all' line, so the page says four types consistently.
Link 'Our separate guide to the Notice of Intended Marriage' to that guide, since it is the next question a reader has.
Split the long Wedded Advisor sentence in the overseas section into two short sentences and say in a few words who the Wedded Advisor is before naming them.

checks.check: Every journey point and turn-off has an exact quote from the draft
Stayed in character as Priya, a casual Google searcher on a phone
No invented brand facts; missing info went to unanswered_questions
Journey types limited to gained_trust, lost_trust, confused, bored, excited, objection
Deferred business details and transfers, deliberately absent prices and celebrant names not treated as must-fix; no request for sourcing explanations
